answers.answer: In the 3-player case, the tied leaders receive no coin, and the unique last player pays 1 coin. In an unequal 2-player Census, the unique leader gains 1 coin, but the last player never pays.
answers.evidence: Census: a tied lead gives no coin; a unique last player pays; in a 2-player game the last player never pays.

answers.answer: No. You may draw up to six but are limited by the two free Market spaces, so at most two. Undrawn Followers already on your Market remain there between rounds and occupy capacity.
answers.evidence: Followers: draw any number up to allowance, limited by free Market spaces; unused Market Followers remain and occupy capacity.

answers.answer: Yes, you may fill an action over multiple rounds, but cannot execute it until all required spaces are occupied by Followers or legal Technology (Town Hall is the stated exception). You may save a fully activated action for a later round. When an ordinary action is executed, its Followers return to your bag; Technology stays on its spaces.
answers.evidence: Planning: may fill gradually; activation requires all spaces; an activation can be saved. Actions: return Followers used for an ordinary action to your bag; Technology stays.

answers.answer: Starting with Start Player, players go clockwise repeatedly and take one activated action or pass on each turn. Passing ends your participation for the Action Phase; you cannot act again that round. An unused activation keeps its Followers on the board for future rounds.
answers.evidence: Actions: one activated action or passing per turn; passing ends participation; unused activations keep their Followers on the board.

answers.answer: Farm House recruits a Farmer into your bag, advances your Farmers Track one space, and gives you the good depicted at that track space.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Farm House: put a new Farmer in your bag; advance Farmers Track one space and take its depicted good.

answers.answer: Village recruits one of a Boatman, Craftsman, or Trader; the chosen neutral Follower goes into your bag and advances that profession's track. Boatman gives the depicted coins (or a Citizen instead at the last space to the first player there); Craftsman gives a Technology tile; Trader gives one Place Tile (category I on the first advance, I or II on later advances).
answers.evidence: Village recruitment: put chosen neutral Follower into your bag and advance its profession's track; Boatman coins/Citizen, Craftsman Technology, Trader Place Tile.

answers.answer: No. Technology gained from the newly recruited Craftsman is used only after you pass, so it cannot help another action during that Action Phase before then. Your first Technology must replace a Farmer. Later Technology can replace any profession except Monk; at most one Technology per Place, none at a Place requiring only one Follower, it cannot be moved, and it stays in place after execution.
answers.evidence: Craftsman: use Technology only after you pass. Technology: first replaces Farmer; later any except Monk; never more than one at a Place or at a one-Follower Place; cannot be moved.

answers.answer: No. The first Trader-track advance permits category I only. Every later advance permits category I or II. Players may inspect the Place Tile stacks at any time.
answers.evidence: Trader: first advance permits category I only; every later advance allows I or II. Setup says players may inspect stacks at any time.

answers.answer: University recruits a Scholar into your bag, advances the Scholars Track one space, and gives the depicted Development Points. Castle recruits a Knight into your bag and advances the Knights Track one space; the first player to the fourth-Knight space takes its Citizen. Monastery recruits a Monk into your bag with no extra track reward. The fourth Knight leaves draw allowance at 7, without increasing it at that step. Once a character track reaches its last space, you cannot take that corresponding action again.
answers.evidence: Actions table and Castle rewards; Character-track limits: cannot take corresponding action once on last space.

answers.answer: Yes, a Monk may replace a Knight (or any other profession) on an ordinary action. No Knight or Technology can replace a required Monk. A Monk also cannot substitute for an exact profession required on Beneficial Deeds.
answers.evidence: Monks: on ordinary actions, a Monk can replace any other profession; reverse forbidden. Deeds require exact professions; substitutions including Monks cannot replace them.

answers.answer: One Ship or Wagon action moves your Merchant along exactly one adjacent Waterway or Road, respectively. You may take at most one good from that connection, even if two are there. An empty connection is legal and yields no good.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: one action traverses just one connection; may take one good; empty Roads/Waterways are legal and yield no good.

answers.answer: Guildhall builds one Trading Station in the town where your Merchant is currently located. A town with any player's station cannot receive another station, except Orléans, where each player may build one station.
answers.evidence: Building: Guildhall requires your Merchant in the town; no station where any player's station exists; Orléans exception allows one per player.

answers.answer: Scriptorium gives 1 Development Point (moves your marker one space). Moving onto or past a coin space gives its depicted coins; the first player onto or past a Citizen space collects that Citizen; reaching or passing a Development Status space immediately changes your Status to the shown value.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Scriptorium; Scoring: on moving onto or past coin collect coins, first onto/past Citizen collects it, Status changes on reaching/passing its space.

answers.answer: Town Hall activates with one or two eligible Followers; you may send one or both. The four marked starting Followers cannot be used. Send each permanently to a free Beneficial Deed space matching its exact profession, which can be on different Deeds; take the depicted 1, 2, or 3 coins for each placement, or for Canalization choose 1 coin or 1 Development Point. Whoever fills a Deed's last space takes its Citizen.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: one or two neutral Followers, not marked starting Followers; exact matching spaces; rewards including Canalization; last space filled awards Citizen.

answers.answer: Pilgrimage forbids Monk recruitment during the Action Phase (Phase 5), taking effect before the Event Phase. Other events are resolved in Phase 6. Pilgrimage is the opening event: setup puts the lighter Pilgrimage tile on top of the Hour Glass stack.
answers.evidence: Hour Glass: Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5; other events wait until Phase 6. Setup: lighter Pilgrimage placed on top, so round 1 always has Pilgrimage.

answers.answer: Harvest food is grain, cheese, or wine; wool and brocade do not qualify. Paid food goes to the Goods Market. If you have no food, you owe 5 coins; if unable to pay that, torture applies for the shortfall.
answers.evidence: Harvest: pay one grain, cheese, or wine to the Goods Market; if unable pay food, pay 5 coins; inability causes torture; wool and brocade are not food.

answers.answer: A neutral Scholar drawn in Plague returns to its game-board supply and becomes recruitable; its track marker does not move back. If the drawn tile is your marked starting Trader, you keep it, lose no Follower that round, and do not redraw.
answers.evidence: Plague: neutral Follower returns to supply; do not move track marker back. Marked starting Follower is kept; no loss and no redraw.

answers.answer: Pay the one coin you have, then cover the two-coin shortfall with two items in any mix from the listed choices: a built or unbuilt Trading Station; one random eligible Follower drawn only from your bag; one Development Point; one Goods Tile; one Place Tile; or one Technology tile. Market/Action Space Followers are ineligible, and marked starting Followers are returned/redrawn until an eligible neutral one is drawn. A lost Development Point moves one space left but never onto or past a coin space. Surrendered items are removed from the game.
answers.evidence: Torture: pay available coins and replace each missing coin with one listed item; Follower drawn only from bag; Development Point moves left but never onto/past coin; items removed.

answers.answer: You cannot play an action that provides an unavailable Character, Technology, or Goods Tile, even if another part of the action would still give a reward. It becomes available again as soon as its required tile returns to availability, subject to normal requirements. If the common supply lacks enough coins, players cannot receive coins at that moment.
answers.evidence: Limited supplies: cannot play action providing unavailable tile; action becomes available when tile is available again; insufficient coin supply means no coins received at that moment.

answers.answer: A tie for most built stations awards the set-aside Citizen to nobody. Final goods values are grain 1, cheese 2, wine 3, wool 4, brocade 5 points each. Score built stations and collected Citizens as (stations + Citizens) × final Development Status. Ties go to the player furthest ahead on the Development Track; if still tied, share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory: unique most stations gets set-aside Citizen; tie gives nobody; table lists values and formula; tie-break on Development Track then shared victory.

answers.answer: Each player receives a board, bag, Merchant, 10 Trading Stations, 5 coins, 7 markers, and four marked starting Followers. Starting Followers go on the Market; Merchant goes in Orléans; one marker goes on the first space of each of six Character Tracks and the Development Track; coins and unbuilt stations are kept in front of the player. The youngest player takes the Start Player token.
answers.evidence: Setup: personal components and their placements; youngest player takes Start Player token.

answers.answer: Place 13 Citizens on their marked board/Deed spaces and set the remaining Citizen aside for the final Trading Station award. Sort neutral Followers by profession into game-board buildings; put Technology in its supply and coins nearby. Separate Place Tiles into categories I and II (inspectable). Shuffle map goods face down, deal one face up to each eligible Road/Waterway goods space (all such spaces in a 4-player game), and sort remaining goods face up into the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1, 3, and 5: Citizens, neutral Followers, Technology, Place Tile stacks, and random map/remaining goods.

answers.answer: For 3 players remove 2 neutral Farmers, Boatmen, Craftsmen, and Traders of each profession; 3 neutral Knights, Scholars, and Monks of each; and 6 random goods; leave spaces marked 4 empty. For 2 players remove 4 of each neutral Farmer/Boatman/Craftsman/Trader; 6 of each neutral Knight/Scholar/Monk; and 12 random goods; leave spaces marked 3 or 4 empty. Remove all starting Followers of unused colors.
answers.evidence: Fewer players table and note: remove all starting Followers of unused colors.

answers.answer: Farm House: Boatman + Craftsman. Village: Farmer + Boatman + Craftsman. University: Farmer + Craftsman + Trader. Castle: Farmer + Boatman + Trader. Monastery: Scholar + Trader.
answers.evidence: Actions table lists required professions before substitutions or Technology.

answers.answer: Ship: Farmer + Boatman + Knight. Wagon: Farmer + Trader + Knight. Guildhall: Farmer + Craftsman + Knight.
answers.evidence: Actions table lists required professions before substitutions or Technology.

answers.answer: Scriptorium requires Knight + Scholar. Town Hall allows 1 or 2 eligible Followers; the detail specifies neutral Followers and excludes the four marked starting Followers.
answers.evidence: Actions table: Scriptorium Knight + Scholar; Town Hall: 1 or 2 eligible Followers. Town Hall detail defines eligibility.

answers.answer: Yes. You may decline two draws and instead move two Followers from Action Spaces back to your Market. You may not move a Follower directly from one Action Space to another.
answers.evidence: For each draw declined, may move one Follower from an Action Space back to Market; this is the permitted recovery method, not direct Action Space transfer.

answers.answer: Yes, you may inspect your bag at any time, but must shuffle its contents afterward.
answers.evidence: Followers phase: may inspect your bag at any time, but shuffle its contents afterward.

answers.answer: The phases are Hour Glass, Census, Followers, Planning, Actions, Event, Start Player. At the end, pass Start Player to the player on your left. Planning is simultaneous; announce completion and, if order matters, plan clockwise from Start Player. Event payments and any necessary order-sensitive resolution are clockwise from Start Player. Paid coins go to the common supply; received coins come from it.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists seven phases and specifies Start Player, Planning order, event order, and coin supply directions.

answers.answer: You do not score immediately. Finish the entire round in which the 18th Hour Glass tile is drawn, including that round's event; then the stated end-game scoring occurs.
answers.evidence: Scoring: finish the entire round in which the 18th Hour Glass tile is drawn, including its event.

answers.answer: The player uniquely ahead on the Farmers Track gains the Census coin, regardless of how many Farmer tiles are in the players' bags.
answers.evidence: Census compares markers on Farmers Track regardless of Farmer tiles in bags; unique leader gains 1 coin.

answers.answer: Income pays coins equal to your current Development Status.
answers.evidence: Events table: Income—gain coins equal to Development Status.

answers.answer: With eight goods, pay 2 coins (one per complete group of three, rounding down). Goods types do not change the count. If you lack the coins, the shortfall causes torture.
answers.evidence: Taxes: count all goods; pay 1 coin per complete group of 3 (round down); a shortfall causes torture.

answers.answer: You receive 4 coins, one per built Trading Station; the six unbuilt stations do not count.
answers.evidence: Trading Day: gain 1 coin per built Trading Station; only built stations count.

answers.answer: Hayrick: Farmer; 1 grain from Goods Market. Cheese Factory: Farmer + Farmer; 1 cheese from Goods Market. Winery: Farmer + Trader; 1 wine from Goods Market. Wool Manufacturer: Boatman + Trader; 1 wool from Goods Market. Tailor Shop: Scholar + Trader; 1 brocade from Goods Market. Each cannot be used when its particular good is absent from the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles table lists costs and goods from Goods Market; following sentence says a goods-producing Place cannot be used when its good is absent.

answers.answer: Shipping Line: Boatman, gain 1 Development Point. Brewery: Monk, gain 2 coins. Windmill: Craftsman + Craftsman, gain 2 coins and 1 Development Point. Library: Knight + Scholar, gain 2 Development Points.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles table.

answers.answer: Any one Follower activates Pharmacy. Pay 1 to 3 coins, advancing one Development space per coin; paying two advances two spaces. Zero or four coins is not allowed.
answers.evidence: Pharmacy: any 1 Follower; pay 1–3 coins; advance one Development space per coin; minimum 1 and maximum 3.

answers.answer: Cellar: Monk + Scholar, gain 4 coins. Office: Scholar + Scholar, gain 1 coin per built Trading Station. Hospital: Boatman + Scholar, gain coins equal to your current Development Status.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles table lists costs and rewards.

answers.answer: Horse Wagon requires Trader + Knight; it moves along one Road to an adjacent town and collects one good if available on that connection.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles table, Horse Wagon.

answers.answer: Laboratory requires Scholar + Craftsman and gives a Technology tile, subject to normal placement constraints. Your first Technology cannot be placed there because it must replace a Farmer. A later Technology can go on either of its spaces if none is already there and the usual constraints are met.
answers.evidence: Laboratory entry: Scholar + Craftsman; gain Technology; first cannot go there because spaces are not Farmer; later may go on either space if none already there.

answers.answer: Bathhouse requires a Farmer. Draw three Followers from your bag, choose two, and immediately place the chosen tiles on appropriate Action Spaces; none can go on the Bathhouse. Return the third drawn Follower and the activating Bathhouse Follower to your bag.
answers.evidence: Bathhouse entry: Farmer; draw 3, choose 2 and immediately place on appropriate Action Spaces; none on Bathhouse; return third and activating Follower.

answers.answer: Place the one drawn Follower that can legally go on an allowed Action Space. Return the other two drawn Followers and the activating Bathhouse Follower to your bag. If none can be placed, return all three drawn Followers and the activating Follower to your bag.
answers.evidence: Bathhouse: if only one or none can legally be placed, do so and return all other drawn Followers to the bag; the activating Follower also returns.

answers.answer: It may be executed on a later action turn in the same Action Phase, if you have not passed: Phase 5 lets you take one activated action per turn, and you choose your action order freely. The newly supplied Follower completes the Place's required spaces, activating it.
answers.evidence: Actions phase: take one activated action per turn and choose actions' order freely; Planning defines activation as filling all required spaces. Bathhouse immediately places drawn Followers on Action Spaces.

answers.answer: Sacristy requires a Monk. If activated, during Phase 6 you return its Monk to your bag instead of suffering a negative event, such as Harvest, Taxes, or Plague.
answers.evidence: Sacristy entry: Monk; protection during Phase 6 against a negative event such as Harvest, Taxes, or Plague; return Monk to bag.

answers.answer: No. Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during the Action Phase (Phase 5). Sacristy protection is used during Phase 6, so it does not override that earlier restriction.
answers.evidence: Pilgrimage restriction applies during Phase 5; Sacristy protection is used during Phase 6.

answers.answer: Herb Garden lets Boatmen replace Craftsmen, Traders, and Farmers on ordinary actions. It does not allow replacing Knights, Scholars, or Monks.
answers.evidence: Herb Garden: Boatmen may replace Craftsmen, Traders, and Farmers on ordinary actions.

answers.answer: School lets Scholars replace other professions except Monks on ordinary actions. It requires no activation. A Scholar cannot replace a required Monk.
answers.evidence: School: no activation; Scholars may replace other professions except Monks on ordinary actions.

answers.answer: No. Beneficial Deed spaces require exact professions, and substitutions including Place abilities cannot replace them. Gunpowder Tower does not change that rule; its Deed spaces still require exact types.
answers.evidence: Town Hall: substitutions including Place abilities cannot replace exact Deed professions; Gunpowder Tower: Deed spaces still require exact types.

answers.answer: Gunpowder Tower adds 2 Market spaces. During Phase 3, put 1 or 2 drawn Followers there. During Planning, move one or both to Action Spaces; alternatively, during Actions send one or both directly to Beneficial Deeds in one action. Two may go to Deeds in that one action if eligible and matching free spaces exist. Marked starting Followers cannot be sent, and Deed spaces require exact professions.
answers.evidence: Gunpowder Tower entry specifies +2 capacity, timing, one-or-both options, direct Deed action, and starting-Follower/exact-type limits.

answers.answer: The unique leader gains 1 coin. The two tied furthest behind are tied for last, so neither pays.
answers.evidence: Census: unique leader gains 1 coin; tied last place pays nothing.

answers.answer: The player with the unique most built Trading Stations receives the set-aside Citizen after the full round 18 is completed, before scoring. It counts as a collected Citizen in the stations-plus-Citizens scoring formula.
answers.evidence: Scoring: finish round with 18th tile; before scoring, unique most stations takes set-aside Citizen; built stations and collected Citizens use the final scoring formula.

answers.answer: Remove the lighter Pilgrimage tile, shuffle the other 17 Hour Glass tiles face down, then put that Pilgrimage on top. In Phase 1, the Start Player reveals the top tile.
answers.evidence: Setup Hour Glass preparation; Phase 1 says Start Player reveals top tile.

answers.answer: Each remaining coin scores 1 victory point.
answers.evidence: Scoring table: Coins—1 each.

answers.answer: Development Status starts at 1 and initial Knight-track draw allowance is 4.
answers.evidence: Setup: Development Status starts at 1; initial draw allowance is 4.

answers.answer: Only lost Development Points can be regained. Surrendered Goods, Followers, Trading Stations, Place Tiles, and Technology are removed from the game rather than returned to their supplies.
answers.evidence: Torture: items surrendered are removed from game; only lost Development Points can be regained.

answers.answer: You may choose the execution order freely; it need not follow printed board order or the order actions were filled.
answers.evidence: Actions: choose your actions' order freely.

answers.answer: Its passive substitution ability is available immediately, including during the current Action Phase; you need not wait until next round.
answers.evidence: Trader recruitment: acquired Place and its passive special ability are available immediately, including during current Action Phase.

answers.answer: You may send just one, or both; it is optional to send one or both in a Town Hall action.
answers.evidence: Town Hall: in one action, send one or both; the action can activate with one or two eligible Followers.

answers.answer: You may complete the move and leave the good there. The rule says you may take one good, so taking it is optional.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: you may take one good from the connection.

answers.answer: Yes. You may send the second on a later action turn in the same Action Phase before passing; they need not be transferred in one action.
answers.evidence: FAQ: Town Hall's two Followers may be sent in separate action turns during the same Action Phase, before passing.
